content: A pocket mask, also known as a pocket face mask or CPR mask, is a medical device designed to safely deliver rescue breaths to a patient experiencing cardiac arrest or respiratory arrest. The pocket mask is compact and portable, making it easy to carry. It functions by allowing the emergency responder to exhale air into the patient through a one-way filter valve. Modern pocket masks are equipped with either a built-in one-way valve or an attachable, disposable filter. Many pocket masks are also equipped with an integrated oxygen intake tube. This feature enables the delivery of oxygen concentrations ranging from 50% to 60% when connected to an external oxygen source. Even without an external oxygen supply, the exhaled air from the responder, which contains approximately 16% oxygen, can still provide sufficient oxygen to sustain life. For reference, the Earth's atmosphere contains about 21% oxygen. Although a pocket mask is less efficient than a bag valve mask in delivering ventilation, it offers certain advantages, particularly in situations where only one rescuer is available. Operating a bag valve mask requires two hands—one to maintain a proper seal on the patient’s face and the other to compress the bag. In contrast, the pocket mask allows the rescuer to use both hands to stabilize the patient’s head. This is especially beneficial when performing a jaw thrust maneuver on a patient with a suspected spinal injury, as it helps maintain proper airway alignment while minimizing the risk of further spinal damage.
